description: Golden reference for calc_accel_magnet.py on the ELF CEFC-2020 C-yoke quarter-xz reproduction (em_elf_quarter_xz.jou + em_elf_coil.py).
rationale: PHYSICS-ACCURACY benchmark vs the published ELF reference (Bz = -228.1 mT at origin, NI=2000, mu_r=1000, IMA='+x-z').  FEM Omega + 5mm tetmesh on the unioned ELF yoke geometry + ELF racetrack coil (Y_CENTER=131.25 mm) reproduces Bz to within 5.2% (-240.0 mT FEM vs -228.1 mT ELF).  Locks the whole physics chain: ELF .meg-derived yoke, ELF coil, sym_bn=0_x + sym_ht=0_z BCs, Auto-Kelvin with kelvin_reduction = {x: bn=0, z: ht=0}.

sample.generator_cmd_note: Regenerate via Cubit batch with kelvin_reduction = {'x': 'bn=0', 'z': 'ht=0'} -> export netgen order=2 overwrite.  Requires the ELF .meg at S:/ELF_MAGIC/2020_03_07_CEFC_2020/model_C-Type/mu=1000/ELF_MMB8T_EIEM2_1x1x1/quater/ELF_magic.meg or override via ELF_MEG_PATH env var.

geometry_note: Yoke: 13 ELF hex CAD volumes UNITED into 1 -> tetmesh at 5 mm.  This trades exact 13-hex topology for face-conformality (per-volume hex meshing fails: imprint+merge is 'overconstrained' for slanted hexes, and per-volume equivalence misses coincident nodes due to heal-perturbation).  Air: full sphere intersected with octant brick (x>=0, z>=0).  Kelvin: full sphere offset along +y, webcut at x=0/z=0 to give 1/4 Kelvin; Kelvin pair 1585/1585 at machine precision.

elf_reference.source: C-type electromagnet quarter model, nonlinear steel reference

fem_convergence_note: Empirical sweet spot (2026-04-25): 5mm + order=1 = 5.2% high; 2mm + order=1 = -22% (DIVERGES with finer mesh); 5mm + order=2 = -39% (broken: C++ Kelvin pair ID only handles LINEAR nodes, periodic BC fails for the high-order DOFs of curvedelements).  Both refinement paths need future fixes before this can converge to <1%.  Until then -- 5.2% is the practical ceiling for FEM Omega + offset-Kelvin on this geometry.

observations.note: FEM result vs ELF: -240.02 mT (FEM) vs -228.1 mT (ELF) = 5.2% deviation.  See fem_convergence_note for refinement caveats.
